## About the course

Generative AI is used increasingly in research, yet its environmental costs, training data, labor conditions, discriminatory representations, commercial incentives, and governance structures are often considered separately. This workshop combines four critical lenses with practical risk-analysis tools. Participants investigate the design, data, training, deployment, evaluation, and governance of text- and image-generating systems; then use two Panarchy blocks to identify feasible changes in their own research environments. Each participant leaves with an individual Action Plan. The aim is a defensible, transparent approach to responsible generative AI use rather than a universal list of permitted and forbidden tools.

## Editions

One set of teaching materials serves every edition. The practical facts differ for each edition.

{{< edition all list >}}

This site is a course companion. It takes no registrations and awards no credits. The Graduate Center (GRACE) of the University of Basel does both. For registration, credits, and the binding course rules, go to the official course listing of the University of Basel. Each edition page links it.

## Start here

### If you take part in a course edition

1. Open the page of your edition above. It gives the date, the venue, and the rules.
2. Read the required text before the course day: Bender et al., [On the Dangers of Stochastic Parrots](https://doi.org/10.1145/3442188.3445922) [-@bender2021].
3. Prepare your Research Use: one actual or planned use of generative AI in your research. The [assignments](contents/assignments.qmd) page explains it.
4. Bring a laptop.

::: {.callout-important title="Protect your data"}
Do not bring confidential or personal research data to the exercises. No exercise needs a commercial AI account.
:::

### If you teach or study on your own

- The [syllabus](contents/syllabus.qmd) shows the learning path and the timetable.
- The four lens pages each hold concepts, evidence, a documented case, and four guiding questions for the Lens groups.
- The [facilitator guide](contents/panarchy-facilitator.qmd) gives the course day minute by minute, with the trainer timeline.
- The [handouts](contents/resources.qmd) are printable and editable.
- The [reuse guide](documentation/reuse.qmd) explains how to adapt the site for your own course.

## Four lenses

| Lens                                                                         | Guiding question                                                                   |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [1. Stochastic Parrots: Scale and Environment](contents/lenses/01-scale.qmd) | Which environmental and data choices are hidden by a model's apparent performance? |
| [2. Representation and Displacement](contents/lenses/02-representation.qmd)  | Whose perspectives become normal and whose are displaced?                          |
| [3. Lifecycle and Labor](contents/lenses/03-lifecycle-labor.qmd)             | Who does the work, carries the risk, or has no recourse?                           |
| [4. Political Economy](contents/lenses/04-political-economy.qmd)             | Which incentives preserve an unsafe or inequitable practice?                       |

: The four analytical lenses {.striped}

After the lenses, Lens groups apply the guiding questions to the participants' Research Uses. In the afternoon, [Panarchy](contents/panarchy.qmd) shows how changes at different levels interact. Each participant leaves with an individual Action Plan.
